chief_complaint: Worsening shortness of breath and fatigue over the past week, especially with exertion.
doctor_notes: Patient is a 68-year-old female with a history of CHF, HTN, and T2DM presenting with worsening dyspnea on exertion and orthopnea. Vitals show elevated BP and HR. Physical exam reveals bilateral crackles at lung bases and peripheral edema. Labs confirm elevated BNP and A1c. Current medications appear to be managed suboptimally. Plan to adjust diuretic dosage and re-evaluate antihypertensive regimen. Patient needs close monitoring for fluid balance and cardiac status.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: Good morning, Eleanor. What brings you in today?

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: Doctor, I've been feeling so tired lately, and I'm getting out of breath even when I walk to the mailbox. My ankles are swollen too.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: I understand. Your vital signs are a bit elevated today, and your lungs sound congested. We'll do some tests to get a clearer picture.

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: Is this related to my heart condition?

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: It's likely a combination of factors, including your heart function and possibly your diabetes. We'll review your lab results and adjust your medications to help you feel better.

conversation_summary.speaker: Patient
conversation_summary.text: I just want to be able to do my daily activities without feeling so weak.

conversation_summary.speaker: Doctor
conversation_summary.text: We'll do our best to get you there. We'll also schedule a follow-up appointment to monitor your progress.

follow_up_actions: Monitor daily weight and fluid intake/output
